_note: Draft English rendering of Saadia's JA Tafsir on Shemot 37, generated by scripts/translate_tafsir_english.py against the JA (not the biblical Hebrew). Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And Bezalel made the ark from acacia wood: two cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
translations.2: And he overlaid it with pure gold, from within and from without; and he made for it a border of gold, encircling all around.
translations.3: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and set them on its four sides — two rings on one side of it, and two rings on the other side.
translations.4: And he made carrying-poles from acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.
translations.5: And he inserted the poles into the rings, on the two sides of the ark, so that it might be carried by them.
translations.6: And he made a cover of pure gold: two cubits and a half its length, and a cubit and a half its width.
translations.7: And he made two cherubim of gold — solid he made them — from the two ends of the cover.
translations.8: One of them from its right side, and the other from its left side — from the body of the cover itself he made them, from its two ends.
translations.9: And the two cherubim were spreading their wings upward, sheltering with them over the cover; and the face of one was toward the other, and toward the cover were their faces turned.
translations.10: And he made the table from acacia wood: two cubits its length, and a cubit its width, and a cubit and a half its height.
translations.11: And he overlaid it with pure gold, and made for it a border of gold, encircling all around.
translations.12: And he made for it a rim of the breadth of a fist, encircling all around; and he made for it a border of gold for its rim, encircling all around.
translations.13: And he cast for it four rings of gold, and set the rings on its four sides — which were at its four legs.
translations.14: Alongside the rim were the rings — a place for the poles — so that the table might be carried by them.
translations.15: And he made the poles from acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold, so that the table might be carried by them.
translations.16: And he made the vessels that were upon it — the dishes, the drawers, the spoons, and the flagons with which it is covered — of pure gold.
translations.17: And he made the lampstand of pure gold — solid he made it: its base and its shaft, its cups, its pomegranates, and its blossoms were all of it.
translations.18: And six branches extending from its sides — three branches from one side of it, and three branches from the other side.
translations.19: Three cups fashioned in almond-shapes on each branch, a pomegranate and a blossom — thus he made it for the six branches extending from it.
translations.20: And in the body of the lampstand itself, four cups fashioned in almond-shapes, with their pomegranates and their blossoms.
translations.21: And a pomegranate beneath each two branches of it — thus for the six branches extending from it.
translations.22: Its pomegranates and its shaft were of it — all of it was one solid piece of pure gold.
translations.23: And he made for it seven lamps, and its tongs and its fire-pans of pure gold.
translations.24: From a talent of pure gold he made it — it and all its vessels.
translations.25: And he made the altar of incense from acacia wood: one cubit its length and one cubit its width — square — and two cubits its height; its horns were of it.
translations.26: And he overlaid it with pure gold — its top and its walls all around, and its horns; and he made for it a border of gold, encircling all around.
translations.27: And two rings of gold he made for it beneath its border, on its two sides — thus on its two sides — as a place for the poles, so that it might be carried by them.
translations.28: And he made the poles from acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.
translations.29: And he made the consecrated anointing oil, and the pure incense of resins — the work of a perfumer.
